brief: UBS's CIO GWM briefcase covers the Fed's September decision: the FOMC unanimously raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, its first hike in three years, with Chair Warsh calling it removal of "a dose of accommodation" amid solid growth. Sixteen of 18 participants see at least one more hike in 2026, with the median dot at 4.1%. UBS itself expects only one further 25bp hike in December, versus markets pricing three more by end-2027, arguing the Fed's own model shows 50bp of extra tightening would cut growth by only a few tenths of a point. Because UBS forecasts S&P 500 earnings up 25% in 2026 and 14% in 2027 (median company growing around 14%), it expects equities to absorb the higher yields, so it stays constructive on equities (diversify, trim single-stock concentration) while also rating fixed income Attractive, favoring investment-grade issuers at medium maturities and shorter-dated exposure in higher-risk credit, but staying cautious on the longest maturities. Supporting evidence cited: eight months of factory-activity expansion, 6.6% nominal GDP growth, and the historical pattern that downturns have not begun until at least two years after Fed hiking cycles start.
